2026 Paris Motor Show • Project KO11 Is Proof That Geely Wants To "Knock Out" Range Rover, Launches Next Year in Europe
Mazda Soul Red Sedan Virtually Steals the Cuorerosso From Alfa Romeo, Hopefully the Hybrid V6 Too
7 photos
Photo: lsdesignsrl / Instagram
Back in September, the French-Italian-American carmaker Stellantis firmly announced its intention to rule the 2026 Paris Motor Show taking place between October 12 and 18 at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles in France with over 60 show vehicles, nine of them being concept cars.
The company even organized a ‘The Night Before’ event, like in the golden old days of automotive shows before the pandemics, and showcased the most important six concepts ahead of the press day to steal the red carpet’s spotlight. They were right to do so because they had cool things to showcase: the Citroen 2CV Concept, a preview of the upcoming return of the iconic 2CV made as an accessible, fully electric model.
There were also the DS F3VER design-led concept to explore the future of the DS Automobiles specialty brand with a possible return of the DS3 model, the ultra-quirky Fiat Multiplay, which reimagined the much-chagrined Multipla as a morphing truck-minivan, the Opel STX dedicated to the revival of the station wagon sector, plus the Peugeot RCZ Vision based on the new STLA One platform.
However, one of the concepts topped all the others – and not because they were uncool. Instead, Alfa Romeo has returned to its former glorious self with the Cuorerosso, a concept car that will probably never morph into a series production model unlike the other five, but nevertheless is painstakingly showing that Alfa still has the design knowledge of making astonishingly beautiful cars.
This ‘sedan’ with a shifting paint – red, of course – has a striking structural feature: the door layout. Like the new Genesis GV90 Neolun , we are dealing with a B-pillarless design and coach rear doors. Also, very importantly, the concept previews an electrified revolution for the iconic 2.9-liter twin-turbocharged V6 engine used in the Quadrifoglio models, mixed with Alfa Romeo's Q4 all-wheel-drive system and a lightweight carbon fiber driveshaft.
If Stellantis dared to put the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso right now into production, it would immediately clash with the likes of the Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, Ferrari Luce, as well as the newly announced Jaguar Type 01, providing a hybridized alternative to the new crop of ultra-luxury high-performance sedans!
Too bad that Stellantis won’t dare that, right? Well, some folks have found other solutions – including a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. More precisely, Luca Serafini, a virtual automotive designer based in Modena, Italy (aka ' lsdesignsrl ' on social media), has imagined an unofficial, hypothetical Mazda sedan as an alternative to the Alfa Romeo Cuorerosso.
The pixel master basically hijacked the stunning design of the Alfa Romeo concept car and swapped the ‘scudetto’ front fascia with the characteristic visage of Mazda models, modifying the LED headlights in the process to better harmonize with the rest of the body of the coach-door sedan. Around the back, the changes are minimal, with the Mazda script instead of Alfa Romeo and a single smaller exhaust instead of the double one used by the Italian concept car.
Mazda has some great powrtrains, but Alfa's hybrid V6 would be an even better fit inside the belly of this streamlined beast, especially if the Italians push the electrified package to more than 700 combined ponies, right? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Luca Serafini (@lsdesignsrl)
